text:
maria: Quick FYI — onboarding run for a community 'Asterion-lite' variant. After int4 conversion we see a weird drop in token-level entropy for the LM head vs fp16 baseline (~0.48 -> 0.31 avg over eval set). Suspect rotary/head-scale mismatch rather than tokenizer, but want to surface here. Repro steps below.

chris: Can you paste the quant config and export flags?

maria: Sure — conversion command we used:```bash
python convert_model.py --src asterion-lite/fp16 --out asterion-lite/int4 --quant bits=4,group=128,method=awq --rotary-scale auto
python run_eval.py --model asterion-lite/int4 --dataset redwood-small-eval --mode lm_eval
```
Outputs: avg_entropy_fp16=0.48, avg_entropy_int4=0.31, ppl_fp16=12.3, ppl_int4=19.8. Also noticed a headwise variance: heads 0-7 drop more.

ben: headwise drop suggests per-head rotary amplitude mismatch. Some converters map rotary freq per-head differently (gemma/qwen exports we saw earlier). Did you check head_dim vs exported rot_freq shape?

maria: Good call. Export metadata shows rot_freq shape matches (num_heads, head_dim/2) but the values look scaled — integer rounding in the quant kernel? Example excerpt:```json
"rotary_freq_sample": [0.9992, 0.9993, 1.0001, 1.0015, ...]
```
Not huge but could multiply across layers.

alice: Did you try forcing "rotary_scale=1.0" in the runtime (override auto) to compare? Also try disabling per-head rotary variation if available.

maria: I ran two quick ablations this morning:
- override rot_scale=1.0 at runtime -> entropy_int4_up_to=0.39 (ppl=15.6)
- run int4 but with per-head rot disabled (global rot only) -> entropy_int4_up_to=0.44 (ppl=13.1)
So looks like per-head rotary scaling + quantization noise interact badly.

chris: Interesting. That points to the quantization of the rotary weights or the applied sin/cos multipliers being inconsistent between export and runtime. Could also be kv cache alignment if low-entropy tokens get cached incorrectly.

maria: I verified kv cache alignment by running short vs long context and comparing logits — cache mismatch not obvious. Logs: "cache_miss_rate=0.004" on both fp16 and int4.

ben: Next step: reproduce in fp16 runtime but apply fake-int4 noise to rotary matrices (simulating quantization) to isolate whether the rotary terms alone cause the drop. If that reproduces, it's rotary quantization artifact.

maria: I'll run a quick perturbation test. Plan: take fp16 weights, quantize only rotary proj matrices to int4 (same grouping) and run eval. If entropy drops, file a kernel/quant bug.

alice: Also record token-level diffs for a handful of prompts (top-5 logits) — helps triage whether probability mass collapses systematically to certain tokens (vocab-related) or is general.

maria: Good idea. Sample diff: prompt "Climate change" top token probs fp16 vs int4-rot-only: fp16 top1=0.12, int4-rot-only top1=0.31 (same token), top5 entropy drop concentrated on top1 increase.

chris: That looks like overconfidence introduced by rotary perturbation. Could be scaling/normalization bug post-rotary application (we do a scale by sqrt(head_dim) in some kernels). Check whether the runtime applies the same norm as the export.

maria: Kernel check: runtime kernel commit shows `apply_rotary(q,k,scale_factor)` where scale_factor defaults to sqrt(2/head_dim) for compatibility with older models. Export metadata didn't include a required flag. Opening PR to log explicit rotary_norm in exports.

deploy-bot: Deployed job run-4923456801 started on infra-ci (cpu: small, gpu: v100).

ben: If experiments confirm, mitigation options: 1) patch runtime to apply per-head rescaling compensation when rotary_quant detected, 2) re-export with 'disable per-head-rot' for int4 artifacts, or 3) adjust quant scheme (bfloat16-ish for rotary) — 1) seems quickest.

maria: Update: perturbation test done — quantizing rotary projections alone drops entropy to 0.33 (close to full int4). So rotary quantization is major factor.

alice: Can you attach the small script and the sample diff outputs? Put in /tmp/ and ping eng-ml thread.

maria: Pushed scripts and raw diffs to s3://redwood-ml/tmp/asterion-rot-qa/ and added short notebook with plots. TL;DR: per-head rotary values amplified by quant grouping causing a few heads to dominate.

chris: Ok, let's do short-term: add a calibration pass that rescales rotary tables post-quant to match original spectral norm per-head. If that recovers entropy we can roll into converter.

maria: I'll prototype calibration and post quant re-scaling — will report numbers here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
